target_customer: Manufacturers, utilities and energy operators and the integrators who build their plant control systems
problem: Industrial control and monitoring runs on legacy SCADA such as Ignition, WinCC and FactoryTalk. Control Seat offers an AI native SCADA and predictive maintenance layer that can replace or sit on top of them.
business_model: Software plus hardware sensors and paid integration services; pricing not published
product_category: AI native SCADA and predictive maintenance for industry

founders.name: Warren Shepard
education: Dartmouth, class of 2026, computer science and mathematics

founders.name: Jack Grodnick
education: Dartmouth, class of 2026, computer science and economics, on leave

competitors.name: Ignition (Inductive Automation)
competitors.traction_then: announced Ignition 2027 with an AI framework called Catalyst

competitors.name: Tatsoft FrameworX
competitors.what: SCADA platform marketed as AI native with MCP servers
competitors.traction_then: named a Visionary Leader in the 2026 Frost Radar for SCADA

competitors.name: WinCC and FactoryTalk
competitors.what: Legacy SCADA platforms from Siemens and Rockwell named by Control Seat as targets

technical_complexity.rationale: Industrial protocols, safety and uptime expectations, own wireless sensors and an LLM layer are hard for a two person team, although the founders have SpaceX and Tesla controls exposure.

defensibility.rationale: SCADA is deeply embedded once installed, but entrants must displace entrenched integrators and Ignition is adding AI itself.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents announced AI features during 2026. No acquisition of Control Seat found.

market_need_then: Control Seat says it spoke with hundreds of hours of controls engineers, manufacturers and integrators and already built a full SCADA system. Plants rely on legacy systems, but no spend data was found.

brand_strength.rationale: Name evokes the operator's chair and fits the product, but no press about the brand or community was found.

pivots.to: Added integration services and predictive maintenance with own sensors
pivots.why: Launch post says the team recently expanded into integration services; the website emphasizes predictive maintenance. Exact dates not stated.

outcome_analysis: Two Dartmouth students incorporated Control Seat in January 2026 and joined YC Summer 2026. They sell AI native SCADA and predictive maintenance against entrenched vendors that are adding AI. It is too early for an outcome. Execution with integration services will decide whether they win first customers.
notes: CB Insights lists a 500 thousand dollar convertible note from YC, a single aggregator figure not recorded as a round; the Dartmouth article says YC invests 500 thousand dollars in each accepted startup, which is the standard deal. YC page says founded 2025 while Dartmouth says incorporated January 2026. Round added: CB Insights convertible note of $500K from Y Combinator, year 2026, a single database; consistent with the standard YC deal described by Dartmouth.
